title: CommonReel: a shared movie-night record
text: CommonReel helps two to four adults choose a movie together. Friends share tonight's time limit and streaming platforms, combine genre vetoes and known watched films, and save a group-recorded choice. This demonstration uses a constructed group in the real running web application.

title: Shared inputs; separate decision versions
text: Each person joins with a nickname. Anyone with the room invite can record inputs for another member. That convenience does not prove personal consent. Go keeps room revisions separate from decision versions, so input changes invalidate old responses while one person's response does not erase everyone else's.

title: A real local model and real MCP calls
text: The assistant runs a local Qwen model through Ollama. It reads the room and calls the actual MCP server to change an explicit member's veto. There is no paid model API. The forms remain available while inference runs. Tool calls and rejected operations are visible, rather than replaced with a scripted success message.

title: Optional CSV; watched does not mean liked
text: This optional import uses a constructed Netflix-format CSV fixture, not a real person's history. One movie matches, one duplicate is removed, and unmatched titles remain pending. A colon does not prove that a title is an episode. Reusable profiles retain normalized inputs with a recovery code; raw CSV is not stored.

title: Verified facts before recommendation scores
text: The bounded catalog contains 217 Wikidata movies with checked identifiers and runtime units. Real Watchmode requests supply United States listings. Only selected subscription platforms qualify. Unknown data, rentals, purchases and hard-limit failures are excluded. Go produces the ranking and displays verified tool facts; model-written platform claims are not trusted.

title: Responses, freshness and a durable choice
text: The page proposes a candidate and records a response for every member entry. Saving is unavailable while a response is missing. Before saving, the server refreshes the chosen film's supply outside the database write transaction, then checks the current versions. A stale decision is rejected. Repeating the same decision reuses its anonymous receipt.

title: Evidence and limits
text: This is an Alexa-plus web simulation with a working self-hosted MCP server over Streamable HTTP, protocol 2025 dash 11 dash 25. Browser synchronization and a narrow layout were checked. A physical phone was not tested, and there have been no human group trials. Subscription listings do not guarantee personal account rights. The code, tests and separated real-run evidence make these limits reviewable.
